position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the West Division block bounded by Randolph, Jefferson, Washington and Des Plaines; standing ON the Randolph Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it
position.note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_west_randolph_des_plaines, the block's Randolph Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its west wall is fixed by the west end of the run's own frontage, 1.5 m clear of the side lot line at that end. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Randolph Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

fabric_basis.words: patched boards under a patched roof — a carpenter's shop, from the 1832–33 town (rule F-W: a tradesman's shop by its type)

frontage.why: T-0024 sends a workshop to its block's better face, and this block's better face is Randolph Street, the ordinary road west out of the town, while every West Division lot fronts the north-south street on the outer side of its column. So the carpenter's or joiner's shop does not stand on a lot frame at all: it stands in a one-lot frontage run on the Randolph face of plat lot 2, against the Des Plaines corner and on the street line, at the 1.5 m margin the plat module allows, because the placement policy's mechanics_streets clause stands a workshop at its street, where a wagon bringing timber or a customer coming out along Randolph meets it first. The run is one lot long and holds one roof; nothing is built shoulder to shoulder here, and the rest of the face stays as open as the recipe's outer edge requires.
